title: Pathwise uniqueness for rough Heston volatility
aliases: Strong uniqueness for the rough CIR process
statement: For the fractional kernel $K_H(t)=t^{H-1/2}/\Gamma(H+1/2)$ with $0<H<1/2$, prove or disprove pathwise uniqueness among nonnegative continuous adapted solutions of $V_t=V_0+\int_0^t K_H(t-s)\kappa(\theta-V_s)\,ds+\int_0^t K_H(t-s)\xi\sqrt{V_s}\,dW_s$. Two solutions on the same filtered probability space, driven by the same Brownian motion and with the same initial variance, must be indistinguishable if uniqueness holds.
assumptions: Fix deterministic V_0 >= 0 and positive kappa, theta and xi; require the stochastic convolutions to be well defined on every finite horizon.
Include the attainable zero boundary rather than assuming variance stays bounded away from zero.
Keep the genuinely singular fractional kernel and square-root diffusion; regularized kernels, Lipschitz coefficients and uniqueness in law are different conclusions.
physics_motivation: Determines whether the rough Heston variance is unambiguously determined by its noise, supporting strong simulation, coupling and sensitivity analysis for derivative pricing.
resolution_target: A pathwise-uniqueness theorem for the full stated fractional square-root regime, or an admissible same-noise counterexample; a positive result should explain the resulting strong-solution construction.
status_note: Weak existence and uniqueness in law are available from affine Volterra theory. General singular-kernel uniqueness results impose coefficient assumptions that do not settle the rough square-root endpoint. The Pannier–Jacquier 2019 preprint claiming rough-Heston strong uniqueness was withdrawn in 2020 because of an erroneous inequality. The 2026 boundary-behaviour preprint studies hitting zero and boundary atoms, not pathwise uniqueness. This entry retains the general fractional square-root question provisionally; it does not treat the withdrawn claim as a proof.

title: Well-posedness of unregularized stochastic local volatility models
statement: Establish sharp, verifiable conditions for existence and uniqueness of the unregularized calibrated dynamics $dS_t/S_t=\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}(t,S_t)\sqrt{V_t/\mathbb{E}[V_t\mid S_t]}\,dW_t$, coupled to a continuous stochastic variance factor V. Determine when the law-dependent leverage coefficient is well defined and the stock-price marginals agree with those of the prescribed local-volatility model, including variance factors that can approach zero.
assumptions: Work under a risk-neutral measure with zero rates and dividends for the displayed equation; prescribe a positive regular local-volatility surface and initial joint law.
Specify the continuous variance-factor SDE, correlation, coefficient growth and boundary conditions; distinguish weak existence, uniqueness in law and pathwise uniqueness.
Interpret conditional expectation through the joint law and require positivity wherever the denominator is used. A fixed positive denominator floor or kernel smoothing changes the problem.
Impose the integrability and true-martingale conditions needed to identify European option prices from the marginals.
physics_motivation: Provides a mathematical foundation for combining an observed vanilla-option surface with stochastic volatility dynamics used to price and hedge exotic derivatives.
resolution_target: A well-posedness and marginal-calibration theorem for a clearly specified class with continuous, possibly degenerate variance factors, or counterexamples locating the necessary restrictions; if regularization is used, justify its removal.
status_note: Regularized equations have well-posedness and particle-convergence results. Mustapha's 2024 strong-existence/uniqueness result assumes a finitely valued volatility factor; other existence and stationary special-case results also exist. The remaining target is a sharp theory for unregularized continuous-factor models, not a claim that all LSV models lack solutions. Source abstracts were checked; no exhaustive 2026 status certification is asserted.

sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: regularization, well-posedness and propagation of chaos.
sources.note: Explicitly distinguishes the unresolved original equation from the regularized model.

sources.title: Reisinger & Tsianni: Convergence of the Euler–Maruyama particle scheme for a regularised McKean–Vlasov equation arising from the calibration of local-stochastic volatility models
sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: strong convergence with fixed regularization parameters.
sources.note: Convergence for a regularized scheme does not establish the zero-regularization limit.

sources.title: Mustapha: Strong existence and uniqueness of a calibrated local stochastic volatility model
sources.locator: arXiv abstract: finitely valued factor assumption.
sources.note: A solved restricted model; the title should not be read as a general continuous-factor theorem.

relations.note: Rough variance could be an additional modelling layer, but its pathwise uniqueness is a separate Volterra problem.
Both concern matching marginal laws while controlling dynamics; a calibrated LSV process is not automatically a Markovian mimicking solution in the stock variable.

title: Sharp conditions for multidimensional Markov martingale mimicking
statement: For a continuous-time family of integrable probability measures $(\mu_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, increasing in convex order, identify sharp additional conditions guaranteeing a Markov martingale M with $\operatorname{Law}(M_t)=\mu_t$ for every t. Determine which regularity, support or nondegeneracy assumptions allow exact mimicking without altering the prescribed marginals.
assumptions: Fix the time regularity of the marginal family, moment bounds and the desired path class, such as cadlag martingales or continuous Ito diffusions.
State whether ordinary Markov or strong Markov behaviour is required; exact prescribed marginals must be distinguished from Gaussian-regularized ones.
Convex-order monotonicity alone is insufficient in multiple dimensions; seek additional hypotheses and examples demonstrating their sharpness.
physics_motivation: Identifies when a dynamically consistent multi-asset martingale model can reproduce prescribed joint distributions across maturities, a basic calibration question for model-independent finance.
resolution_target: A checkable existence theorem for a nontrivial class of exact multidimensional marginals, paired with counterexamples or necessity results explaining which assumptions cannot be removed.
status_note: The unrestricted multidimensional extension is false. Pammer, Robinson and Schachermayer give counterexamples and construct strongly Markovian mimicking Ito diffusions after Gaussian regularization. The open research target concerns optimal hypotheses for exact marginals in a fixed process class; it does not ask for a proof of the disproved unrestricted statement.

sources.title: Pammer, Robinson & Schachermayer: A regularized Kellerer theorem in arbitrary dimension
sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: Gaussian regularization theorem and multidimensional counterexamples.
sources.note: Supports both the obstruction and the restricted positive result; exact optimal hypotheses require further research.

sources.title: Beiglböck, Huesmann & Stebegg: Root to Kellerer
sources.locator: One-dimensional Kellerer theorem.
sources.note: Background on the real-line theorem; not evidence for an unrestricted higher-dimensional extension.

relations.note: Mimicking asks for a Markov process with given time marginals; martingale transport optimizes a payoff over admissible couplings and need not impose Markovianity.

title: Extremal structure and certified bounds in multidimensional martingale transport
statement: For vector-valued asset prices at finitely many dates, characterize the geometry of martingale laws that maximize or minimize the expected value of a specified multi-asset payoff subject to marginal constraints. Develop convergent computational constructions of these extremal laws and matching sub- or superhedges, with certified errors for the resulting model-independent derivative bounds as discretization is refined.
assumptions: Specify whether the data fix full joint asset marginals at each date or only each asset's individual marginals; these define different feasible sets.
Assume a nonempty class of integrable martingale laws, and fix payoff continuity or semicontinuity, growth and moment conditions.
Use at least two assets; specify the time grid, asset dimension and payoff family when seeking structural or complexity theorems.
State admissible static option positions and predictable dynamic strategies in the dual hedging problem; do not assume dual attainment without its hypotheses.
physics_motivation: Turns observable option-price constraints into rigorous bounds for multi-asset exotic derivatives without choosing a single calibrated stochastic model.
resolution_target: New structural characterizations for a specified multidimensional payoff/marginal class and an algorithm with matching primal-dual certificates and a proved continuum error bound; explain dependence on dimension and number of dates.
status_note: Existence, duality and extremal-support results are known in substantial regimes. Ghoussoub, Kim and Lim establish higher-dimensional structural results under specific hypotheses. Che, Lim and Sun's February 2026 preprint reports multi-period, multi-asset dual attainment under regularity and irreducibility assumptions, with discrete computations. The remaining target is broader extremal geometry and certified scalable approximation; it does not label general duality or the cited attainment theorem as unsolved.

sources.title: Ghoussoub, Kim & Lim: Structure of optimal martingale transport plans in general dimensions
sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: increment-modulus costs, dual attainment and extreme-point support results.
sources.note: The structural conclusions depend on dimension, marginal order and regularity.

sources.title: Che, Lim & Sun: Dual Attainment in Multi-Period Multi-Asset Martingale Optimal Transport and Its Computation (2026 preprint)
sources.locator: arXiv abstract: regularity/irreducibility conditions and discrete PDLP experiments.
sources.note: Recent preprint claim; the abstract was checked, not the full proof or continuum numerical error.

relations.note: Shares convex-order marginal constraints, but optimizing a coupling is different from constructing a continuous-time Markov martingale.
Both require dimension-aware guarantees for stochastic optimization; their constraints and dual formulations differ.

title: Nonlinear market impact without price manipulation
aliases: No dynamic arbitrage with nonlinear transient impact
statement: Characterize nonlinear transient-impact dynamics with stochastic, state-dependent liquidity for which every admissible self-financing round trip has nonnegative expected execution cost relative to the unaffected price. Seek conditions compatible with concave volume response and impact decay, specifying how trading changes the impact state and how that state changes execution prices.
assumptions: Take the unaffected price to be a martingale under the evaluation measure and require predictable strategies with zero terminal net inventory and sufficient integrability.
Fix trading-rate or variation constraints, the execution-price convention, initial impact state, spread and fees; include any terminal liquidation or stored-impact value consistently.
Focus on stochastic, endogenous liquidity or nonlinear state evolution beyond fixed deterministic-kernel composition laws already classified; make the additional dynamics explicit.

Separate no profitable expected round trips from absence of transaction-triggered manipulation and from pathwise nonnegative costs. Empirical calibration is a motivation, not a mathematical resolution criterion.
physics_motivation: Prevents an execution or liquidity-risk model from rewarding artificial buy–sell cycles while retaining realistic nonlinear price response and recovery.
resolution_target: Necessary and sufficient no-manipulation conditions for a specified nonlinear stochastic-liquidity class, with nontrivial admissible constructions and counterexamples outside those conditions.
status_note: Gatheral established restrictions connecting impact nonlinearity and decay. Lee's September 2026 preprint claims extensive classifications for deterministic memory models: rigidity when nonlinearity acts before memory, and complete-positivity criteria when a monotone readout acts after memory. It also treats specified time-inhomogeneous and matrix settings. Those claims narrow the target; this entry concerns further stochastic/endogenous-liquidity dynamics, not the old deterministic power-law parameter region. The 2026 classification is attributed as a preprint claim, not independently proof-verified here.

sources.title: Gatheral: No-dynamic-arbitrage and market impact
sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: no-dynamic-arbitrage restrictions on impact and decay.
sources.note: Foundational restrictions; later work changes which deterministic cases remain unresolved.

sources.title: Lee: Price manipulation in nonlinear transient impact models: rigidity before memory and complete positivity after memory (2026 preprint)
sources.locator: arXiv v1 abstract, submitted 2 September 2026.
sources.note: The order of nonlinearity and memory matters. The catalog does not independently certify this preprint's proofs.

relations.note: Once admissible impact dynamics are fixed, optimal execution can lead to nonlinear stochastic-control equations.
Endogenous liquidation prices also drive fire-sale feedback, although equilibrium selection is a distinct question.

title: Provably efficient solvers for high-dimensional fully nonlinear HJB equations
aliases: Curse of dimensionality in stochastic control
statement: Identify broad, explicitly structured families of controlled diffusions whose fully nonlinear HJB equation $\partial_t u+\sup_{a\in A}\{b^a\cdot\nabla u+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\sigma^a(\sigma^a)^\top D^2u)+f^a\}=0$, with terminal condition $u(T,\cdot)=g$, admits an implementable solver with proved error and computational cost polynomial in state dimension and inverse accuracy. Include control-dependent diffusion and quantify the cost of optimization or training, rather than only proving that a small approximating network exists.
assumptions: Specify coefficient/payoff representations, their dimension-dependent regularity constants, control-set complexity, horizon and access to simulation or coefficient oracles.
Fix an error norm and domain or sampling distribution, and include the success probability for randomized algorithms.
Assume comparison and well-posedness for the chosen viscosity-solution class. Restrict input structure enough to avoid hiding exponential complexity in the data.
Separate representation, discretization, sampling and optimization errors; a numerical benchmark or an infinite-width limit is not a finite-runtime guarantee.
physics_motivation: Would make high-dimensional portfolio allocation, optimal execution and hedging computations reliable through explicit accuracy and resource guarantees.
resolution_target: An end-to-end polynomial-complexity theorem for a financially meaningful fully nonlinear class beyond existing restricted results, or a complexity lower bound under an explicit input and algorithm model locating the boundary of tractability.
status_note: Convergent probabilistic methods and dimension-independent approximation results exist under structural assumptions. Grohs–Herrmann study a restricted control-affine, quadratic-cost class. Hutzenthaler–Nguyen's 2025 result shows a curse of dimensionality for full-history recursive multilevel Picard approximations on one HJB example; it is not an impossibility theorem for all solvers. The unresolved target is efficient end-to-end computation for further specified fully nonlinear classes.

sources.title: Fahim, Touzi & Warin: A probabilistic numerical method for fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs
sources.note: Foundational probabilistic approximation framework for fully nonlinear equations; convergence is distinct from dimension-polynomial cost.

sources.note: Approximation/representation result for a restricted class; not an unrestricted training-time guarantee.

sources.title: Hutzenthaler & Nguyen: Full history recursive multilevel Picard approximations suffer from the curse of dimensionality for the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation of a stochastic control problem
sources.locator: arXiv abstract: lower bound for the named MLP approximation method on an example equation.
sources.note: The obstruction is method- and problem-specific.

relations.note: Recursive-utility optimization produces nonlinear HJB or BSDE characterizations, but verification and efficient numerical solution are separate tasks.
Both seek certified high-dimensional stochastic optimization under different modelling constraints.

title: Equilibrium selection in financial networks with defaults and fire sales
statement: In a financial network with interbank liabilities, default losses and endogenous fire-sale prices, determine which static price-payment equilibrium is selected by an explicitly specified dynamic clearing and liquidation mechanism. Characterize its convergence and basins of attraction, and whether the selected equilibrium is stable under small liquidity shocks, asynchronous updates or vanishing adjustment frictions.
assumptions: Fix network liabilities and seniority, external assets, recovery/default-cost rules, liquidation constraints and the inverse-demand or price-impact map.
Choose a setting known to admit multiple static equilibria; specify initial conditions, information, timing and the adjustment dynamics that define selection.
State the order of long-time, small-noise and vanishing-friction limits when these are used, and allow for nonconvergence or mechanism-dependent limits.
Computing the greatest or least fixed point alone is not a prediction of which equilibrium a dynamic mechanism reaches.
physics_motivation: Explains when balance-sheet contagion and forced asset sales lead to different systemic outcomes from the same static network, improving the interpretation of stress tests.
resolution_target: A selection and stability theorem for a specified network/adjustment class, identifying the limiting equilibrium and its basin, or counterexamples demonstrating persistent cycles or dependence on the mechanism and limit order.
status_note: Static existence and algorithms for greatest/least price-payment equilibria are established in integrated default-cost, fire-sale and cross-holding models. Dynamic clearing frameworks also have existence and uniqueness results under their own assumptions. The research question is the relation between specified dynamic mechanisms and multiple static equilibria; there is no mechanism-free universal selection rule asserted here.

sources.title: Weber & Weske: The joint impact of bankruptcy costs, fire sales and cross-holdings on systemic risk in financial networks
sources.locator: Scholarly abstract: existence of price-payment equilibria and greatest/least equilibrium algorithms.
sources.note: Static extremal equilibria do not by themselves resolve dynamic selection.

sources.title: Banerjee, Bernstein & Feinstein: Dynamic clearing and contagion in financial networks

sources.note: A specific dynamic framework; its uniqueness is not a universal selection result for all fire-sale models.

relations.note: Fire-sale inverse demand and transient execution impact both model endogenous prices; consistency requirements differ across the two settings.

title: General Epstein–Zin optimization in incomplete markets
statement: Characterize well-posedness, optimal consumption/investment and value-function regularity for Epstein–Zin stochastic differential utility in incomplete markets with stochastic investment opportunities, across preference and market regimes not covered by existing verification theorems. Determine conditions ensuring a uniquely specified utility process, a finite value, an attained optimum and a valid HJB or BSDE characterization, especially on an infinite horizon.
assumptions: Specify risk aversion gamma > 0, elasticity of intertemporal substitution psi > 0 and discounting; treat gamma = 1 or psi = 1 as explicit limiting cases rather than silently substituting into singular formulas.
Fix traded assets, unhedgeable factors, coefficient growth, admissible portfolios and consumption, solvency constraints and the utility solution concept.
Distinguish finite-horizon terminal conditions from infinite-horizon transversality; state which sign and integrability class selects the recursive utility solution.
Select concrete preference/coefficient regimes beyond the cited results before attempting a theorem; do not assume arbitrary parameter choices yield finite utility or unique BSDE solutions.
physics_motivation: Supports portfolio and consumption decisions when risk aversion and willingness to shift consumption across time are separate, while investment risks cannot all be hedged.
resolution_target: Sharp well-posedness and verification conditions for a specified additional incomplete-market class, with existence of admissible optimizers and uniqueness/regularity in the stated solution class, or counterexamples identifying necessary preference and growth restrictions.
status_note: Many restricted problems are solved. Xing gives a BSDE characterization when risk aversion and elasticity of intertemporal substitution both exceed one under the paper's assumptions. Bayraktar–Lawless's 2026 preprint develops infinite-horizon variational verification in the regime theta=(1-gamma)/(1-1/psi) in (0,1). Ho's July 2026 preprint gives another infinite-horizon HJB construction under its own hypotheses. The target is a broader classification beyond covered regimes; it is not a claim that incomplete-market or infinite-horizon Epstein–Zin optimization is wholly open. Recent abstracts were checked, without a complete theorem-by-theorem scope audit.

sources.note: Established restricted-regime verification, not a general all-preferences theorem.

sources.locator: arXiv abstract: limits of bounded-domain HJB solutions and explicit solutions in some regimes.

relations.note: A verification theorem identifies the correct nonlinear control equation; the HJB problem separately asks how to solve such equations with certified computational cost.

title: Endogenous Market Efficiency Under Long-Memory Order Flow
aliases: Adaptive liquidity under persistent order flow
statement: Research program: construct and analyze an endogenous market in which institutional order splitting produces persistent signed order flow with $C_{\varepsilon}(\tau)\sim c\tau^{-\gamma}$, $c>0$ and $0<\gamma<1$, while strategically adapting liquidity providers generate asymptotically Brownian transaction prices. Derive quotes, inventory adjustment and price impact from agent objectives and interaction rules, without postulating an efficient-price process or tuning a prescribed impact kernel to cancel order-flow persistence. A central target is the functional limit $(p_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}-p_0)/\sqrt n\Rightarrow\sqrt{D}B_t$ with $D>0$, for the resulting zero-drift price observable. The new contribution must extend the assumptions or conclusions of existing propagator, nonlinear-impact, Hawkes and arbitrageur microfoundation models.
assumptions: Specify institutional metaorder sizes, arrival and splitting rules, and establish persistent order flow from these primitives; correlation decay alone does not determine the process law or imply a central limit theorem.
Fix liquidity providers' information, utility or profit criteria, inventory penalties, capital constraints, competition and learning rules, together with the equilibrium or adaptation concept.

Define transaction price versus midpoint or log-price, trade time versus calendar time, matching rules, tick size and spread. Derive zero drift under stated symmetry conditions or explicitly center by a proved drift before taking the scaling limit.

Seek an invariant regime for returns and the relative order-book/liquidity state, including liquidity-provider inventories where appropriate; the absolute level of a nondegenerate diffusing price is not stationary.

State initial-law, moment and dependence conditions and prove process-level convergence, for example in Skorokhod D([0,T]) with its J1 topology for each finite T, including tightness and a finite positive diffusion coefficient. Linear variance growth or white returns alone does not establish this limit.

For no-manipulation results, specify predictable self-financing round trips, information, admissibility, fees, impact accounting and terminal liquidation. A Brownian limit is distinct from exact martingale efficiency or nonnegative expected execution costs at finite horizons.

The restricted propagator reproduction must fix volume weights, convergence of historical sums or price increments, and any independent noise contribution; an added random-walk component can dominate a subdiffusive impact component.
physics_motivation: Connects nonequilibrium statistical physics and market microstructure by asking how adaptive liquidity transforms persistent institutional trading into diffusive prices, with impact and efficiency emerging from participant interactions.
resolution_target: First milestone (known mathematics): audit the five cited papers at theorem level and formalize $\beta_c=(1-\gamma)/2$ in a restricted discrete-time propagator model, recording its assumptions and noise convention. Original-research targets: T1, construct an economically specified endogenous market and prove existence of a stationary relative-state regime consistent with its equilibrium or adaptation rules; T2, derive the impact response and its scaling from agent strategies; T3, prove the stated nondegenerate Brownian functional limit, including tightness; T4, characterize a parameter/behavior class where diffusion persists, or exhibit failures; T5, establish nonnegative expected impact costs for admissible round trips under explicit accounting. Lean proofs can certify rigorously stated claims; reproducible stochastic simulations support conjecture discovery and counterexample searches. Empirical order-book comparisons assess modelling assumptions separately from the mathematical resolution.
status_note: Exploratory long-horizon research program, not a single established conjecture or an unexplained phenomenon in every model. Bouchaud et al. (2004), section 3.2, equation (23), already derive the critical propagator balance $2\beta+\gamma=1$; reproducing it is not a novel result. Their equation (20) also contains an independent diffusive-noise contribution, so a subdiffusive impact component need not make total prices subdiffusive. Lillo–Farmer document compensation of persistent order signs by volume and liquidity fluctuations. Sato–Fujiwara–Kanazawa's v5 revision (5 November 2026) gives an exactly solvable nonlinear-impact model mapped to a Levy walk and reports diffusive prices under square-root impact. Muhle-Karbe et al. (2026) obtain Hawkes-based scaling limits and relations among flow, impact and rough volatility, using no-arbitrage constraints. Bonart (2026) microfounds diffusive impact with arbitrageurs under asymptotically complete aggregate private information and suitable convergence to a stationary limit. These results substantially overlap the motivation: novelty must be located through a theorem-level audit and explicit extensions, such as finite-information, inventory-constrained adaptive liquidity with proved equilibrium and a robust functional limit. Such extensions are candidate directions, not certified gaps after an exhaustive literature review.
